top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz) has the cleanest credit line on the slate, with a precisely identifiable core in Melitz (2003) and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple. It is more than twenty years old and has been tested on firm-level data in many countries, and it has been extended across trade, macro, development and industrial organisation. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism, with no welfare magnitude and no claim to the exporter-premia facts, handles the uncredited Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum lineage and the functional-form dependence of the welfare gains. I do not think P001 is clearly better than P003 on science alone. The gap is about attribution cleanliness: P003 requires choosing Dorn over Katz and leaves the task-framework credit partly outside the credited names. Its evidence is more directly checkable and its core findings have held up, but its aggregate magnitude and persistence are still debated, so I rank it second. I rank P004 third because its identification is partly observational and it overlaps with the 2024 prize. I rank P002 fourth because any three-person cut among eight credited names is contestable. P000 is last because every proposal is a mature, defensible achievement.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for the credited names on any proposal. Disclosed connections: Lund colleague Tommy Andersson (committee member, prefers P002), and co-authorship ties to Lindvall, Cermeño and the Lund economic-history school, none of whom is credited. My regional-growth and local-adjustment research is thematically adjacent to P003, which is field proximity, not a documented conflict. I applied common criteria across fields.
